item.title: Application and Optimization of the GET Electronics System for Double-Sided Silicon Strip Detector Readout
item.description: arXiv:2610.12923v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Double-sided silicon strip detectors (DSSDs) are widely used for charged-particle detection in nuclear reaction experiments. However, the large number of readout channels associated with DSSDs places stringent demands on front-end electronics and data acquisition systems, particularly in experiments employing large detector arrays. In this work, we investigate the application and optimization of the Generic Electronics for Time Projection Chambers (GET) system for multi-channel DSSD readout. Through optimization of the DC-blocking capacitors on the custom-designed interface board and waveform-based energy extraction algorithms, the readout system achieves an energy resolution of {\sigma} = 22 keV for 5.49 MeV alpha particles. Its performance is further validated in a representative nuclear physics experiment employing charged-particle telescopes. The results demonstrate that the GET system provides a versatile and scalable waveform-sampling solution for multi-channel DSSD readout.

item.title: CNN-based Position Reconstruction for the T0 Detector in the HIRFL-CSR External-target Experiment
item.description: arXiv:2610.12969v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The T0 detector provides the event start time for the HIRFL-CSR external-target experiment, and its multi-channel readout signals also contain 2D position information of incident particles. In the CEE experiment, the dedicated beam-profile detector has a rate capability of only ~1 kHz, far below the beam event rate of up to 1 MHz, so it cannot provide real-time beam-spot monitoring under high-rate data-taking or an event time reference. To fill this gap, this work studies a CNN-based position reconstruction method that enables the T0 detector to provide both start time and beam-spot information. The over-threshold times and time-over-threshold (TOT) values from 32 SiPM channels are reorganized into a geometry-preserving input tensor. Time features are corrected by event-wise mean-time subtraction, and TOT features are normalized by an event-wise trimmed mean before feature standardization. A customized CNN directly regresses the incident coordinates. Training and validation samples are built with Geant4 simulation and waveform digitization, and the method is evaluated using a pulsed-laser scanning data set with known position labels. On independent test sets, the residual standard deviations for uniformly distributed planar simulation data are about 1.11 and 1.04 mm in x and y. For the discrete laser-scanning geometry, the resolutions are about 2.36 and 1.34 mm in simulation and 2.42 and 1.41 mm in experiment. The trained model is applied to CEE zero-field beam data collected at the Institute of Modern Physics, Lanzhou, in January 2026, and a 2D beam-spot distribution is reconstructed. These results show the T0 detector's potential as a high-rate beam-spot monitor while retaining its role as an event start-time detector.
item.dc:creator: Shuai-Ke Lv, D Hu, M Shao, Yingjie Zhou, Yiding Zhao

item.title: Beam Spill Structure Measurements at CEE Using the T0 Detector
item.description: arXiv:2610.13004v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Cooling Storage Ring External-target Experiment (CEE) at the Heavy Ion Research Facility in Lanzhou uses a slow-extracted heavy-ion beam whose temporal profile directly affects detector occupancy. The existing CEE T0 detector, originally designed to provide the event start time, is extended in this work to measure the spill structure immediately upstream of the fixed target. The detector consists of a 0.8-mm-thick EJ-200 plastic scintillator read out by 16 silicon photomultipliers at each end. The SiPM signals are conditioned and discriminated by the NINO front-end electronics, and the resulting timing signals are recorded using an FPGA-based time-to-digital converter. In laboratory tests, with the laser trigger set to its maximum available repetition frequency of 100~MHz, the recorded T0 hit-rate distribution was concentrated around 100~MHz. During the June 2024 beam test with 350-MeV/u Kr ions, the accelerator team varied several operating settings, including RF-KO, sextupole, and feedback settings, while T0 independently recorded the corresponding spill profiles. An empirical representation was used to extract the rise, plateau, and fall durations from the stored profiles. The plateau duration was used as the primary comparison metric while accelerator stability and RF-system load were also considered. The measurements clearly distinguished the spill-profile responses associated with different accelerator settings. The spill obtained with the selected settings exhibited a more nearly rectangular envelope than the initial profile, although residual fluctuations and a terminal spike remained. These results demonstrate that the existing CEE T0 detector can provide independent beam-structure information during accelerator tuning.

item.title: Measurement of the free ion yield and estimate of the electron mobility of Trimethyl-Bismuth (TMBi)
item.description: arXiv:2610.13564v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the physical characteristics of the liquid Trimethyl-Bismuth (TMBi) relevant for charge readout in potential TMBi filled detectors for Positron-Emission-Tomography (PET) instruments. The high photo-efficiency and the possibility of fast timing by detection of Cherenkov light created in the liquid are both favorable for use of TMBi in a PET system. However, to obtain a high position and energy resolution also a readout of the charge signal created due to the absorption of a 511 keV photon is required. For this purpose the liquid has to be clean of electro-negative and ionic impurities. A distillation technique was developed within this study as one of the possible methods to remove such impurities and a measurement on the efficiency of this cleaning method is provided. The relevant quantities for an efficient charge readout are the free ion yield and the electron mobility of the liquid. We report on a new measurement of the zero-field free ion yield in TMBi and, using that result, produce an estimate of the electron mobility. The rather low zero-field free ion yield and its much lower expected electron mobility compared to tetramethyl-n compounds like TMSi question the use of the trimethyl molecule TMBi for a PET detector liquid. But we are also giving arguments that the tetramethyl molecule TMPb could be an interesting alternative.

item.title: A new device for live cell imaging of biological samples under in-plane shear
item.description: arXiv:2610.13496v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The effect of mechanical stresses and deformations upon the behavior and properties of cells and tissues is a topic of paramount interest in the field of biophysics. Its understanding is essential for deepening our comprehension of cellular responses to environmental stimuli, with implications in fields ranging from embryogenesis to tumor development. For boosting the understanding in this field, it is important to develop devices for the application of simple deformations in order to probe the cellular response to the basic mechanical transformations. While a number of stretching devices have been developed, in-plane shearing deformation has been little investigated. Here, a new device is introduced that allows the application of homogeneous in-plane shear upon a cell monolayer while imaging the sample with a commercial optical microscope. A description of the faced experimental challenges is reported and a full characterization is presented. It is demonstrated the capability of the device to apply reproducible, controlled and homogeneous shear of both single cells and confluent cellular monolayers.
item.dc:creator: Sidharth Kumar Das, Lyova Mamoyan, Eberhard Bodenschatz, Stefano Villa

item.title: A machine-learning method for the estimation of the background from jets misidentified as hadronic tau lepton decays
item.description: arXiv:2610.13634v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Backgrounds arising from quark- and gluon-initiated jets misidentified as hadronically decaying tau leptons constitute a major experimental challenge for analyses involving tau leptons. The MUltivariate Fake-Factor INference (MUFFIN) approach, a machine-learning-based method for estimating this background directly from observed events, is presented. Boosted decision tree reweighting is used to learn multidimensional, per-object correction factors directly from observed data, thereby modelling the jet to hadronic tau lepton misidentification probability across the kinematic and topological phase space without relying on low-dimensional parametrisations. Performance studies are presented using proton-proton collision data collected by the CMS experiment at the CERN LHC at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13.6 TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 62.4 fb$^{-1}$. Compared to low-dimensional parametrisation methods, improved modelling of key kinematic observables is achieved, particularly in regions of high $p_\mathrm{T}$. The improved modelling leads to a reduction of up to 70% in the systematic uncertainty associated with jets being misidentified as hadronically decaying tau leptons. The MUFFIN method provides a robust and scalable method for background estimation in precision measurements and searches for beyond-the-standard-model physics involving tau lepton final states.

item.title: The throttling refrigeration system for high cooling power recovery of the PandaX-xT cryogenic distillation system for radon removal
item.description: arXiv:2512.20947v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The PandaX-xT cryogenic distillation system for removing radon (Rn) is designed to operate at a high liquid flow rate of 856 kg/h, equal to 5 liters per minute (LPM), to meet the required Rn concentration. However, it is challenging to maintain a continuous supply of cooling power (20 kW) for the Rn-removal system. This work proposes a throttling refrigeration system to address the power supply problem for the next-generation PandaX-xT dark matter detection experiment. The system utilizes carbon tetrafluoride (R14) refrigerant to recover power based on heat pump principles. The cooling power from the liquid xenon (LXe) in the reboiler at 178 K is transferred to liquefy the gaseous xenon (GXe) in the cryostat through the phase change circulation of R14, enabling xenon (Xe) to return to the detector in the same state as when it was extracted. Consequently, a stable circulation for liquid distillation is established. Given the high cost of Xe, a research and development (R&D) experiment has been conducted to validate the feasibility of this high-cooling-recovery system by using ethanol as a substitute for Xe. Experimental results indicate that the proposed system could achieve a cooling power recovery of 25 kW, with a recovery efficiency of 99%+-0.5%. Additionally, process simulation and optimization of the throttling refrigeration cycle are performed using Aspen Hysys. The deviation between the simulation and experimental results is found to be <3.64%. These findings demonstrate that implementing Rn-removal distillation at a high flow rate is feasible, eliminating the need for liquid nitrogen or cryocoolers. This system could save approximately 3650 m3 of liquid nitrogen per year or reduce power consumption by 230 kW.

item.title: The Instrumented Baffle at the Input Mode Cleaner of Advanced Virgo Plus: Four years of Successful Operation as a Monitor of Stray Light
item.description: arXiv:2603.29873v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The suspended end mirror of the Input Mode Cleaner cavity in the Advanced Virgo Plus interferometer was equipped with an instrumented baffle in Spring 2021, serving as a demonstrator of the technology in preparation for the installation of large instrumented baffles in the main arms of the interferometer. This baffle includes tens of sensors positioned near the mirror to enable monitoring of stray light within the cavity. In this contribution, we assess the stability and performance of the instrument after four years of operation. After introducing the main characteristics of the baffle, we study the distribution of stray light and show that the instrumented baffle can be used to monitor laser stability and alignment within the cavity. Finally, we perform a noise level assessment with data from the final stages of the O4b commissioning and conclude that the baffle does not introduce any additional disturbance to the normal operation of the interferometer.

item.title: Detector Performance and Dark Matter Sensitivity of CYGNO with HFO-1234ze Gas Admixtures
item.description: arXiv:2607.20370v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The CYGNO project develops optical time projection chambers for directional dark matter searches, using a He:CF4 (60:40) gas mixture at atmospheric pressure and a triple-GEM amplification stage. We investigate the addition of 1-10% HFO-1234ze as a hydrogen-containing additive with low global warming potential. The charge response and scintillation light yield are studied with the MANGO prototype, complemented by secondary-scintillation spectroscopy of the baseline mixture and mixtures containing 1% and 2.5% HFO. Increasing the HFO concentration shifts the charge-response curves towards higher GEM voltages and strongly suppresses the scintillation emission in both the ultraviolet and visible bands. We use the measured optical response to estimate the impact on projected spin-independent WIMP-nucleon and spin-dependent WIMP-proton exclusion limits for a CYGNO-like directional detector. Under the assumed detector-response model, the higher optical energy threshold largely outweighs the benefit of the additional light target, although a 1% HFO admixture retains a limited advantage for low-mass spin-dependent interactions. An idealized fixed-threshold benchmark is also considered to illustrate the potential of the modified target composition without the optical threshold penalty.

item.title: Stringent constraints on nonstandard neutrino interactions using high-purity $\nu_{\mu}$ CC events in IceCube DeepCore
item.description: arXiv:2512.22632v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The neutral-current (NC) nonstandard interactions (NSIs) of neutrinos with fermions can modify the flavor oscillations of atmospheric neutrinos as they propagate through the Earth. We present constraints on the NC-NSI parameters $\varepsilon_{\mu\tau}$ and $\varepsilon_{\tau\tau}-\varepsilon_{\mu\mu}$ (one at a time) using a high-purity sample of $\nu_{\mu}$ charged-current atmospheric neutrino events collected by IceCube DeepCore over 7.5 years of livetime. These two parameters significantly affect the $\nu_\mu$ disappearance channel for which this golden event sample is optimized by IceCube Collaboration. The best fit to this dataset is consistent with no NSI hypothesis, and we place the stringent constraints $-\,0.0094 < \varepsilon_{\mu\tau} < 0.0079$ and $-\,0.031 < \varepsilon_{\tau\tau}-\varepsilon_{\mu\mu} < 0.029$ at the 90% confidence level, assuming normal mass ordering.
item.dc:creator: J Krishnamoorthi, Anil Kumar, Sanjib Kumar Agarwalla
